audited_plan.image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a rough, wet rocky substrate. The organism has an elongated oval shape with a dark, leathery girdle surrounding a central series of segmented plates. The surface appears wet and textured.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior end is blunt and indistinct.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the animal blends smoothly into the girdle without a distinct head shape, appearing blunt as expected.
The surface of the head region is uniform with the rest of the girdle; no antennae or eye spots are detected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal surface protected by eight overlapping calcareous plates arranged in linear series.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plates embedded in tough leathery girdle that may be smooth, spiny, or hairy.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates are surrounded by a distinct, textured mantle (girdle) that appears leathery and covers the lateral margins of the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plate coloration ranges from grey, brown, green to mottled patterns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates exhibit a dark, mottled grey-brown coloration that blends with the wet rock environment, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal view; the ventral foot is completely occluded by the body against the rock.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.

The transition between the leathery girdle and the rock substrate is somewhat ambiguous in areas, with minor bleeding that makes it hard to distinguish where the animal ends and the wet rock begins.
